extracted.intended_audience: educators, educational theorists, policymakers, and students of education
extracted.subtask_description: Define and judge the nature and quality of aims in education for a democratic society: how aims should arise, function, and be tested in practice, and how education should serve social and international democratic ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure of a social form's worth
rubrics_metrics.description: The two points selected by which to measure the worth of a form of social life are the extent in which the interests of a group are shared by all its members, and the fullness and freedom with which it interacts with other groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A society is undesirable if it internally and externally sets up barriers to free intercourse and communication of experience. Educational criticism and construction require specifying the social ideal; a democratic society is one that secures participation in its good for all members on equal terms and flexible readjustment of institutions through interaction of associated life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim must be internal to activity (not externally imposed)
rubrics_metrics.description: An aim set up must fall within an activity rather than be furnished from without; aims supplied from outside limit intelligence and are mechanical means to other ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast mere results with ends: an end within activity implies ordered, cumulative process and foresight. Anti-pattern: ready-made, external aims that must be imposed by authority and leave intelligence only mechanical choice of means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim must be an outgrowth of existing conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The aim set up must be an outgrowth of existing conditions; it must be based upon a consideration of what is already going on, upon the resources and difficulties of the situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theories that assume ends lying outside activities violate this principle. Good aims survey present state of pupils' experience and form plans compatible with concrete conditions and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim must be tentative, experimental, and revisable
rubrics_metrics.description: The first emergence of an aim is a tentative sketch; acting upon it tests its worth and it must be capable of alteration to meet circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A valid aim is experimental and grows as it is tested in action. Anti-pattern: rigid, externally established ends that resist revision and attribute failure to perverse conditions rather than to an unreasonable end.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim must represent continuity and cumulative growth
rubrics_metrics.description: An aim implies intrinsic continuity: activities should exhibit time span and cumulative growth rather than being mere serial aggregates of acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If each pupil act is dictated by the teacher and has no internal continuity, speaking of educational aims is nonsense. A genuine aim provides an ordered sequence where each step prepares the next.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim requires foresight and intelligent planning
rubrics_metrics.description: To have an aim is to foresee a future possibility, have a plan for its accomplishment, note means and obstructions—mind is capacity to refer present conditions to future results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foresight functions in three ways: (1) careful observation of conditions and means, (2) suggesting proper order/sequence for using means, (3) enabling choice among alternatives by predicting outcomes. Acting with an aim is equivalent to acting intelligently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim must free activity (activity-as-end)
rubrics_metrics.description: The aim must represent a freeing of activities: the object is a mark by which the mind specifies the kind of activity one desires to carry out; the doing with the thing is the end, not possession of the thing itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid conceiving ends as static possessions imposed from without. The aim should direct and continue purposeful activity (e.g., aiming at a target to exercise marksmanship rather than owning the target).

rubrics_metrics.name: Education should develop personal interest and habits for democratic control
rubrics_metrics.description: A democratic education must give individuals a personal interest in social relationships and control, and the habits of mind which secure social changes without introducing disorder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Education should cultivate dispositions to participate in social life and to manage social change responsibly, rather than merely inculcating obedience or passive acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality of opportunity and institutional provision
rubrics_metrics.description: School facilities must be of such amplitude and efficiency as will in fact discount the effects of economic inequalities and secure to all youth equality of equipment for their future careers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accomplishing democratic aims requires adequate administrative provision, supplementation of family resources, and modification of traditional ideals, subjects, and methods so youth remain under educational influence until prepared to master their economic and social careers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education should promote flexible readjustment of institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: A democratic society requires flexible readjustment of its institutions through interaction of different forms of associated life; education should secure such flexible readjustment rather than freeze institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions must be open to change generated by interaction among social forms; education should develop habits and capacities that enable adaptation without disorder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education must emphasize cooperative, international ties beyond nationalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Education must emphasize whatever binds people together in cooperative human pursuits and results, apart from geographical limitations; the secondary and provisional character of national sovereignty in respect to fuller human association must be instilled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond teaching the horrors of war or avoiding stimuli to animosity, schools should cultivate dispositions and knowledge that favor international cooperation and cosmopolitan elements consistent with democratic aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education must recognize individuality and diversity of capacities
rubrics_metrics.description: Education should recognize the uniqueness and infinite diversity of original capacities in individuals rather than lumping people into a few fixed classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid systems that test and sort individuals into a small number of rigid categories (as critiqued in Plato); democratic education should utilize specific and variable qualities of individuals to foster change and progress.
